blocks.text: 1. Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR)

blocks.alt: The position of the first relevant result gives 1 divided by position, forming the MRR
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785439734656-501633671.png

Recall At K closed by showing recall and precision pulling against each other as K changes. Mean Reciprocal Rank, how quickly the first relevant chunk actually appears across many queries, introduces a metric that finally cares about position within the retrieved set.
It scores each query by one divided by the rank position of its first relevant result, then averages.
2. Neither Precision Nor Recall Care About Position
Both precision at K and recall at K treat every position inside the top K as equal.
Neither metric captures whether the first relevant chunk appeared immediately or barely made the cutoff.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Metric","Cares about position within K"],"rows":[["Precision at K","No, treats every position equally"],["Mean Reciprocal Rank","Yes, position of the first relevant result is the whole metric"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Reciprocal Rank For A Single Query

blocks.alt: A relevant result at position 3 gives a reciprocal rank of 1/3
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785439734657-407655669.png
A single query's reciprocal rank is one divided by the position of its first relevant result.
A relevant result at position one scores a full point, at position four scores one quarter.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A query whose first relevant chunk appears at position three, scores a reciprocal rank of one third, regardless of how many other relevant chunks appear later in the list.
blocks.text: A query whose first relevant chunk appears at position three scores a reciprocal rank of one third, regardless of how many other relevant chunks appear later in the list.
4. Meaning Across Many Queries

blocks.alt: Query 1 reciprocal rank and query 2 reciprocal rank average into MRR
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785439734657-918155910.png
As with averaging precision across many queries in Precision At K, averaging the reciprocal rank across a real evaluation set produces the mean reciprocal rank.
The mean part of the name is not optional; it is the entire point of the metric.
5. MRR Only Looks At The First Relevant Result

blocks.alt: Only the first relevant result counts toward MRR
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785439734658-444968217.png
As with recall needs the entire set of relevant chunks in Recall At K, MRR ignores every relevant chunk after the first one entirely.
A query with ten relevant chunks scores identically to one with just a single relevant chunk, as long as the first appears at the same position.
6. MRR Scores Have A Logical Ceiling And Floor
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785439734658-599638106.png
A relevant chunk always appearing first produces the maximum score of exactly one.
No relevant chunk found at all within the considered results scores exactly zero for that query.

blocks.text: 7. MRR Suits Known Item Search

blocks.alt: Known-item search is compared against exploratory search
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785439734658-883789544.png
As with a question with a hidden dependency chain in Multi-Hop RAG, a query looking for one specific known fact only cares how fast that fact surfaces.
MRR was originally built for exactly this single-answer retrieval scenario.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A question like what is our support phone number has exactly one correct answer to surface quickly, the exact single-answer scenario MRR was designed to measure.

blocks.text: 8. MRR Versus Precision And Recall
As with precision recall tradeoff in practice in Recall At K, precision and recall measure coverage of the retrieved set, while MRR measures speed to the first hit.
Three different lenses on the same underlying retrieval, each answering a different question.
9. Recognizing When MRR Is The Right Metric To Track

blocks.alt: Only one correct answer existing points toward tracking MRR
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785439734659-956753797.png
A system where users want the single best answer fast benefits from tracking MRR.
A system where several relevant chunks all matter should track recall instead.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates computing reciprocal rank per query and the mean reciprocal rank across a small evaluation set.

code.content:
def reciprocal_rank(retrieved_chunks, relevant_chunk_ids):
    # reciprocal rank for a single query
    for position, chunk_id in enumerate(retrieved_chunks, start=1):
        if chunk_id in relevant_chunk_ids:
            return 1 / position
    return 0.0

queries = [
    {"retrieved": ["c1", "c2", "c3"], "relevant": {"c2", "c5"}},
    {"retrieved": ["c4", "c5", "c6"], "relevant": {"c5"}},
    {"retrieved": ["c7", "c8", "c9"], "relevant": {"c10"}},
]

ranks = [reciprocal_rank(q["retrieved"], q["relevant"]) for q in queries]

print("Reciprocal rank per query:")
for i, rank in enumerate(ranks):
    print(f" Query {i + 1}: {rank:.3f}")

# meaning across many queries
mean_reciprocal_rank = sum(ranks) / len(ranks)
print(f"\nMean Reciprocal Rank: {mean_reciprocal_rank:.3f}")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the third query scoring zero because its only relevant chunk was never retrieved at all, exactly the logical floor as MRR scores have a logical ceiling and floor.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Using MRR for a task where multiple relevant chunks all matter, not just the first one.
Reporting a single query's reciprocal rank as if it represents overall system performance.
Confusing MRR with precision or recall, which measure coverage rather than speed to the first hit.
Forgetting that a query with no relevant chunk retrieved scores exactly zero, not undefined.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Mean Reciprocal Rank measures how quickly the first relevant chunk actually appears across queries.
Neither precision nor recall care about position; MRR is built specifically around it.
A single query's reciprocal rank is one divided by the position of its first relevant result.
Averaging reciprocal rank across a real evaluation set produces the mean reciprocal rank.
MRR ignores every relevant chunk after the first one entirely.
MRR scores range from one, first result relevant, down to zero, no relevant result found.
MRR suits known item search, where a query has one specific answer worth surfacing fast.
Precision and recall measure coverage; MRR measures speed to the first hit, three different lenses.
